subject: MSA / Order Form: clarification on credit "slice" model, on-call routing & maintenance carveouts
messages:
From: Sara Ng <sara@atlasdata.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: MSA / Order Form: Support & SLA redlines

Vanessa / Marissa —

Thanks for taking our call earlier. Attached is Atlas's redline to the Order Form and a short spreadsheet that shows how we calculate monthly availability for our internal billing. A few things we flagged that we'd like clarification on before we proceed to a counter: 

- Service credit calculation: your draft applies credits at the tenant level. Atlas needs per-route (API surface) crediting for critical endpoints. Is Redwood open to a "slice-and-apply" approach (credits applied only to impacted routes)?
- Maintenance carveouts: your MSA excludes scheduled maintenance but is unclear about cross-region rolling maintenance and emergency maintenance. We want firm guardrails for notifications and limits on emergency maintenance that affect >5% of capacity.
- On-call / response times: your SLA distinguishes severity levels but the escalation path/after-hours on-call contact was redlined out. Please confirm your standard on-call reachable window and expected initial response times for P1/P2.
- Fallback behavior: Atlas expects automatic degraded routing to an older model variant (lower throughput/cost) rather than outright failures. Can Redwood put that behavior into the Order Form or an ops addendum?

Attaching: Atlas_OrderForm_Redline_v2.docx, redline-comments-ops.xlsx

Can you loop in ops and legal to get a joint position? We want to keep this in the week of Aug 16 so procurement can sign the underlying MSA.

Thanks,
Sara Ng
Sr. Cloud Architect, Atlas Dataworks

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sara Ng <sara@atlasdata.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 08:23:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form: Support & SLA redlines

Vanessa / team / Sara —

Thanks for the packet, Sara. Technical POV below — I've tried to keep options rather than a single hardline so procurement can pick what fits Atlas's risk profile.

1) Slice-and-apply credits (per-route):
   - Feasibility: doable provided Atlas maps "critical routes" to named routes in the Order Form (e.g., /api/v1/ingest, /chat/completions). Our billing and telemetry can compute per-route availability if routes are explicit.
   - Implementation notes: we'll need a one-time mapping doc and Atlas must enable route-level tags in their tenant. Credits are calculated pro-rata to token usage on the impacted route for the month.

2) Maintenance carveouts (scheduled vs emergency):
   - Proposed scheduled window: 02:00–04:00 UTC, rolling by region; customers notified 72 hours in advance for non-urgent maintenance. Up to 4 scheduled events per quarter without crediting.
   - Emergency maintenance: defined as work required to mitigate immediate security/availability risk. We propose the following constraint: Redwood will notify within 1 hour of decision to act, try to limit impact to <5% capacity per region where feasible, and provide a post-mortem within 72 hours. If emergency maintenance causes >5% sustained degradation for >30 minutes, it will be creditable (exception to carveout).

3) On-call and response times:
   - Standard reachable window: 24/7 for Sev1/critical incidents. Initial acknowledge/response target: 15 minutes for Sev1, 2 hours for Sev2. Full triage ETA varies by incident complexity (we'll include runbook TLs).

4) Fallback/degraded routing:
   - We already support model variant fallbacks in our runtime. We can commit to an operational fallback behavior for specific APIs: automatic routing to a pinned lower-tier model when capacity constraints are detected, with a documented latency/cost impact. We prefer to capture this as an "ops addendum" that describes expected behavior, limits, and telemetry (rather than bake deep behavioral guarantees into the SLA).

Next steps: if Atlas accepts the mapping requirement for slice-and-apply credits and the proposed emergency carveout threshold, I can produce a technical appendix (redline) for the Order Form showing the per-route credit calc and required telemetry fields.

-Karthik
VP, Infrastructure — Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.inference>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference>
Cc: Sara Ng <sara@atlasdata.com>, procurement@atlasdata.com
Date: Wed, 12 Aug 2026 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form: Support & SLA redlines

Team / Sara —

Legal position (high level):

- Per-route credits: acceptable so long as (1) Atlas provides explicit route identifiers tied to billing usage, (2) credits do not exceed the monthly invoice for the impacted route, and (3) the Order Form includes the mapping doc as an appendix. We will not accept unlimited micro-slicing; suggest a cap of 10 named routes per agreement or an alternative scale clause.

- Emergency carveout threshold: the proposed >5% sustained degradation for >30 minutes is reasonable, but we need a clear measurement method (rolling 15-minute windows, using our shared telemetry). We'll include language that requires Redwood to publish the post-incident measurement and calculation.

- Fallback ops addendum: OK to keep operational details in an addendum. From a contracting perspective we need a short-service description and a limitation of liability carve specifically stating that degraded routing may change functionality/latency and is not a substitute for full availability guarantees.

I'll prepare redline language for the Order Form and the Ops Addendum. Two asks for Atlas to expedite: (1) provide a list of critical routes you want included and (2) confirm whether you want the 10-route cap waived or prefer an alternate scaling method.

I'll circulate a consolidated counter by EOD Thu (Aug 13) after Karthik's appendix is attached.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Contracts — Redwood Inference
